name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about fifteen points and incumbent Jim Baird is running for re-election
Baird holds a massive financial edge: roughly $582k raised plus $537k in outside support, versus about $54k raised by Drew Cox
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about four percent
No public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Baird's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Cox leave no evidence of a competitive race; markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major national Democratic wave or a late surge of outside spending against Baird would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Jim Baird, the incumbent, is seeking another term with the advantages that come with it: name recognition, a fundraising edge of more than ten-to-one over Democrat Drew Cox, and over half a million dollars in outside support behind his campaign. Cox has raised about $54,000 and enters the fall with little cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings treat this race as competitive, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a four percent chance of an upset. The national political environment could trim a few points from Baird's margin, but the combination of district lean, incumbency, and financial dominance leaves Cox needing a dramatic shift to contend. The seat remains solidly Republican on the current evidence.
